citation.description: registry_drift recorded non-blocking; control falls through to remaining freshness checks. Confirmed by test_compute_validity.py:93-107 and test_attestation_invalidation.py:111-129.

criteria.criterion: A plan-review attestation whose signed `regver` differs from the current `registry_version(repo_root)` returns `valid: True` from `compute_validity`, and the ticket can be claimed without a fresh `review-plan`.

citation.description: _result helper attaches registry_drift dict with signed/current keys when non-None. Tests assert res['registry_drift'] == {'signed': ..., 'current': ...}.

criteria.criterion: The same result carries `registry_drift` with the signed and current stamps, so the drift is reportable rather than silent.

citation.description: test_plan_review_grandfathered_when_regver_missing asserts valid: True and registry_drift == {'signed': None, 'current': 'rv0'}. Also test_attestation_invalidation.py:132-140.

criteria.criterion: A manifest with NO `regver:` line is likewise grandfathered (valid), not rejected.

citation.description: test_regver_drift_does_not_mask_code_drift_on_a_scoped_attestation: one SCOPED attestation signed against 'an-old-registry-version' AND watched_both.py, which is then edited post-signing. Asserts verdict == 'stale-code' plus registry_drift riding along.

criteria.criterion: `stale-code`, `stale-head`, `stale-material` and `stale-reopened` still return `valid: False` — proven by a test that rotates the registry AND drifts a dependency file on one attestation and asserts the verdict is `stale-code`.

citation.description: test_compute_validity_ignores_plaintext_manifest_dep_and_regver_tamper: corrupting plaintext manifest's regver to 'TAMPERED-REGVER' does not surface as registry_drift; 'registry_drift' not in v_tampered asserted.

criteria.criterion: The signed `regver` is read from the authenticated manifest only; corrupting the plaintext mirror does not change the reported `registry_drift`.

citation.description: Status: Accepted; Amends ADR 0015; records 'Accepted cost — a criteria *tightening* no longer applies retroactively.' ADR 0015 also updated with amended-by pointer at line 3.

criteria.criterion: `docs/adr/0053-grandfather-criteria-registry-drift.md` exists, states the amendment to ADR 0015, and records the accepted consequence that a criteria TIGHTENING no longer retroactively forces re-review.
